summary: New ELO-based matchmaking feature (humans-only, no bot fill) verified end-to-end. Added /app/backend/tests/test_elo_matchmaking.py with 5 focused tests: (1) 4 fresh users mm1..mm4 join queue -> found_count grows 1,2,3 with players list carrying username/avatar_id/elo, all four transition to status='found' with the SAME game_id within ~4s of the 4th join; (2) WebSocket to that game_id (with browser UA) yields state.players len==4 and every player is_bot=false; (3) solo user in queue: elo_range starts at 100 and grows to >=200 after ~11s of continued polling; (4) stale purge: solo user stops polling for 15s -> next status is 'idle'; (5) private-room regression: host starts with 1 human -> WS state has exactly 1 human + 3 bots. Full backend suite: 26/26 pass in 37.9s (test_ws_game was skipped from this run because it was flagged flaky in iteration 1 and is unrelated to the new feature). Frontend (Playwright, mobile 390x844): tester1 login, Jouer en ligne -> Partie courte -> matchmaking screen shows '1/4 joueurs', 'Plage ELO ±100' chip, 3 dashed empty slots + own avatar+ELO, timer ticks 3s->6s, ELO chip widens from ±100 to ±150 by 6s (matches +50/5s rule), 'Annuler la recherche' returns to home with no lingering modal. All feature acceptance criteria met.

action_items: None blocking for the ELO matchmaking feature — ship it.
(Carry-over from iter 1) Replace shadow* RN style props with boxShadow and props.pointerEvents with style.pointerEvents to silence console warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: game_manager.queue_status refreshes last_seen only on the caller's own entry — correct (a stale entry never has its last_seen touched by someone else's poll). Good.
elo_window(waited) = 100 + (waited // 5) * 50 — verified in code and observed live (chip went from ±100 at 3s to ±150 at 6s).
_make_match seats players[0], players[1], players[3], players[2] so strongest+weakest are teammates (seats 0 & 2). Balanced-team rule from spec is honoured.
queue_status returns 'idle' when user has neither a matched entry nor a queue row — used by the stale-purge test and confirmed working.
matchmaking_loop purges entries where (now - last_seen) > QUEUE_STALE_SECONDS (12s). Consistent with spec.
Private-room /rooms/{code}/start still calls make_bots for empty seats — regression check passed.
